title: Python Tutorial - Numbers and Arithmetic
text: Python can be used as a calculator. The operators +, -, * and / perform arithmetic, while parentheses group expressions. Division with / produces a floating-point result. Python supports integers, floating-point numbers, Decimal, Fraction, and complex numbers. The built-in round function can round a number to a requested number of digits.

title: Python Tutorial - Strings
text: Strings represent text and can be written with single or double quotes. A backslash introduces escape sequences such as newline. Strings can be concatenated with + and repeated with *. Strings are indexed from zero and support slicing. Python strings are immutable, so changing an indexed character is not allowed; a new string must be created instead.

title: Python Tutorial - Lists
text: Lists are compound data types written as comma-separated values inside square brackets. Lists can contain values of different types, can be indexed and sliced, and are mutable. Slice operations return a new list. Lists support concatenation and methods such as append and extend.

title: Python Tutorial - if Statements
text: An if statement executes a block when its condition is true. It may be followed by one or more elif clauses and an optional else clause. Conditions can use comparison operators such as <, >, ==, <=, >= and !=. Indentation defines the block belonging to the conditional statement.

title: Python Tutorial - for Statements
text: The Python for statement iterates over the items of a sequence or other iterable in the order they occur. The loop body is indented. The range function is commonly used to generate arithmetic progressions of integers. The loop variable receives each item in turn.

title: Python Tutorial - Defining Functions
text: Functions are defined with the def keyword followed by a function name and a parenthesized list of parameters. The function body is indented. A return statement leaves the function and can provide a result. Parameters may have default values, and keyword arguments can be used when calling a function.

title: Python Tutorial - List Methods
text: The list append method adds an item to the end of a list. extend adds all items from an iterable. insert places an item before a specified index. remove deletes the first item whose value equals the argument. pop removes and returns an item, using the last item by default.

title: Python Tutorial - Lists as Stacks and Queues
text: Lists can be used as stacks by appending items and removing the last item with pop. For queues, removing from the beginning of a list is inefficient because all remaining elements must shift. The collections.deque type is recommended when fast appends and pops from both ends are needed.

title: Python Tutorial - Syntax Errors
text: Syntax errors are parsing errors that occur when Python cannot parse a statement. The interpreter reports the offending line and usually points near the location where the parser detected the problem. A missing colon after a compound statement is a common example.

title: Python Tutorial - Exceptions
text: Exceptions occur during execution and can be handled with try and except statements. A try block contains code that may raise an exception, while except clauses specify handlers for particular exception types. A program can also use else and finally blocks. The finally block runs whether or not an exception occurs.

title: Python Standard Library - pathlib
text: The pathlib module provides object-oriented filesystem paths. Path is the concrete path class normally used for the current operating system. Paths can be joined with the slash operator, checked with methods such as exists and is_dir, and traversed with iterdir or glob. Path objects can also open files.

title: Python Standard Library - json
text: The json module provides methods for working with JSON data. json.dumps serializes a Python object to a JSON formatted string, while json.loads parses a JSON formatted string into a Python object. json.dump writes JSON to a file-like object and json.load reads JSON from one.

title: Python Standard Library - re
text: The re module provides regular expression operations. Patterns can be compiled with re.compile and applied to strings with methods such as search, match, findall and finditer. A regular expression describes a set of strings using syntax for literals, character classes, repetition, grouping and alternation.

title: Python Standard Library - datetime
text: The datetime module supplies classes for manipulating dates and times. datetime represents a date and time, date represents a calendar date, time represents a time of day, and timedelta represents a duration. These objects support arithmetic and comparisons useful for application logic.

title: Python Standard Library - Counter
text: collections.Counter is a dict subclass for counting hashable objects. It can be initialized from an iterable or mapping and provides methods such as most_common for retrieving frequently occurring elements. Counter objects are useful for frequency analysis and tallying repeated values.

title: Python Standard Library - deque
text: collections.deque is a double-ended queue with approximately O(1) appends and pops from either side. It supports append, appendleft, pop and popleft. A deque is generally preferred over a list when a program needs efficient operations at both ends.
